summary: The lord of intelligence, children and past merit joins the self, so learning and children become part of the person's identity. Modern authors read it as one of the better placements; BPHS adds a self-interested, calculating streak, and Raman splits the result sharply by the lord's condition.

by_area.personality: Intelligent, kind-hearted and knowledgeable (Rath; Braha). BPHS 24.49 also warns of a miserly, calculating side.

by_area.finance: Braha: wealthy. BPHS 24.49's line about taking others' wealth is a traditional caution.
by_area.relationships: Braha: pleasurable love affairs; happy childhood.
by_area.family: Happiness from children (BPHS 24.49; Braha); Raman: few children, more so if afflicted.
by_area.spirituality: Raman: earns the grace of God. Braha: learned in scriptures, mantras and spiritual techniques; charitable.

lagna_or_context_notes: Functional role (BPHS 34.2-7; Raman, How to Judge a Horoscope pp. 13-15): the 5th lord is a trikona lord and auspicious, and BPHS names the 5th a house 'specially for wealth'. It is a yogakaraka for Cancer (Mars 5+10), Libra (Saturn 4+5) and Capricorn (Venus 5+10). Where it co-owns a difficult house the sources differ: Venus (5+12) is the only benefic for Gemini (BPHS 34.25, Raman) and gives mainly 5th-house results (Frawley); Mars (5+12) for Sagittarius is auspicious (BPHS 34.37, Raman); Jupiter (5+8) for Leo is auspicious in BPHS 34.29 but neutral in Raman; Mercury (5+8) for Aquarius gives mixed effects (BPHS 34.41) and is neutral in Raman; Saturn (5+6) for Virgo is neutral in Raman and less auspicious in Frawley because its mulatrikona sign rules the 6th; Mercury (2+5) for Taurus is 'somewhat inauspicious' in BPHS 34.23 but a benefic in Raman. The lagna is both a kendra and a trikona (BPHS 34.2-7), so a trikona lord here is a classic auspicious link.
